newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma said to free detained NLD leader Kyi Maung.
newsitem.headline: Burma said to free detained NLD leader Kyi Maung.

text.p: Burma's military government on Monday freed Kyi Maung, the deputy chairman of the National League for Democracy (NLD), who was detained last week, NLD sources and a member of his family told Reuters.

Kyi Maung, a confidant and adviser of democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi, was held by the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) on October 23 for questioning over his alleged involvement in a rare student protest. Official confirmation of his release was not immediately available.
"He was returned home at 12.45 p.m. (0615 GMT) today," said a family member by telephone when asked if Kyi Maung had been released.

A government official said Kyi Maung had been held for questioning at a guesthouse since last Wednesday to find out if he had advised two students involved in a demonstration against the SLORC on October 23.
Kyi Maung was seen talking to two students leaders the day before up to 1,000 university students staged the protest about two km (1.2 miles) from Suu Kyi's residence.

Western nations and human rights organisations condemned the detention of the 75-year-old Kyi Maung. The European Commission, in retaliation, had planned to tighten restrictions on visas and high-level contacts with Burma on Monday.
